intro: Long before anyone in India wrote a book, families of priests carried a huge body of poetry in memory. These are the Vedas. Many Hindus regard them as shruti, sacred sound that was heard by ancient seers. Scholars study them as the oldest texts of South Asia, composed beginning around 1500 BCE.

In this unit you will read hymns from the Rig Veda to fire, storm, dawn and sun, including the Gayatri mantra and the creation hymn that ends with a question. Then you will look at all four Vedas, their layers, the fire ritual, and the remarkable ways reciters kept every syllable safe.

By the end, you will be able to name the four Vedas and their layers, explain how Hindus use Vedic verses today, and describe how scholars and Hindu tradition date these texts differently. You will also see how the question of who may learn the Vedas has changed.
bigQuestion: What are the Vedas, and how have Hindus kept them alive and used them for over three thousand years?

write.prompt: Why have the Vedas lasted so long? Cite two or three passages from this unit, such as Rig Veda 1.1.1, 3.62.10 or 10.129.7 (Griffith, 1896), and explain what they say and how Hindus have used and kept them.
tips: Give the Veda, book, hymn and verse, and name Griffith's 1896 translation.
Attribute beliefs: "many Hindus believe" or "scholars date".
Give both scholarly and traditional views of the Vedas' age.
Use unit terms like shruti, mantra, yajna and oral transmission.
